title: Meet Muse: your personal AI agent
format_note: Real users testify to a phone agent in interview and B-roll; interface appears only as brief handheld phone close-ups, with a lower-third naming each person and their Muse.
one_thing: Muse is a personal agent that does the thing for you and asks before it buys, proven by real people describing life moments.

transcript.voice_style: Warm, conversational first-person testimony from several speakers; casual fillers; one founder-style definition line; no narrator.
transcript.script_shape: Cold-open anecdote about mum, definition of Muse, capability claims, then a chain of personal stories (running, car lockout, purchase approval, tickets, credit score, weekend plan), closing on time with loved ones.

copy.holds_vs_reading_rule: Name labels are short (3 words per line) and stay 1-4s; the end card holds about 5s, above the 2s rule. Most of the story is carried by voice, so almost no text is read.

sound.music: Audio kind is music with speech: describe tags speech 0.839, music 0.649, keyboard_musical 0.276, plucked_string_instrument 0.164; no steady beat detected (confidence 0.092), so a soft ambient bed under voices.
sound.sfx: No sound effects identifiable from tags; captions carry [music] cues only.
sound.vo_music_balance: Voices dominate (speech 0.839 vs music 0.649); integrated -17.2 LUFS, short-term max -14.0, true peak -0.8 dBTP, LRA 5.4 LU.
sound.energy_arc: Even testimony level with ten sections A-J; silence only at 108.5s and the last 2.9s before the final fade.
sound.sync_to_picture: Cuts are not locked to the sound: 7.5% of cuts land on strong onsets against 8.4% by chance; cuts follow speech phrases instead.

good.observation: Real people tell personal stories, so each claim lands as lived proof rather than a feature claim; a named lower-third ties each person to their own Muse.
Lower-thirds are one stable template: bold name, lighter line, round avatar; repeated four times so the audience learns the pattern.
The approval beat is shown and spoken together: price, shipping and delivery date, then 'it doesn't actually buy it until I approve it'.
The end card is plain: icon, wordmark, two badges, one parent logo on black, held about 5s.
Frame 0 is a poster-like sunlit frame, then every shot after it is a new composition (91.5% of sampled intervals), so the film never sags.
Split screens at 12-15s combine wide, face and UI so the audience sees who, how they feel and what they see in one beat.

weak.observation: Phone screens are skewed, soft and brief; body text is unreadable at phone width, so the specifics spoken in voiceover are not confirmed on screen.
The hook line is a mum anecdote with no product shown; frame 0 and the first 9s show no interface and no name until the 9.68s tag.
Cuts are not locked to the music, 7.5% on strong onsets vs 8.4% chance.
Loudness is -17.2 LUFS integrated with true peak -0.8 dBTP, quieter than the -14 target and above the -1 ceiling.

rule_candidates.rule: Label each testimonial speaker with a two-line lower-third (name, then 'Muse name is their pronoun Muse') and keep the same template, type size and position across all speakers.
rule_candidates.evidence: Four labels measured 35-45px high at similar x (f0013, f0024, f0031, f0044).

rule_candidates.rule: A launch film built on testimony can sustain a 1.4s median shot for 2 minutes if every cut changes composition and follows a spoken phrase.
Phone UI shown through the user's hand must hold the screen steady for at least 1.5s with the headline text above 4% of frame height, or it reads as texture rather than proof.
rule_candidates.evidence: Goals and Route Map legible only in f0007, f0028; others soft.

rule_candidates.rule: Shown consent beats claimed consent: for any agent action with cost, show price, delivery and an approve step on screen while the line is spoken.
Open on a lived moment without product only when the product tag arrives by 10s; here the Muse tag lands at 9.68s, outside the 3s hook window.
End on a plain black card with icon, wordmark, store badges and parent brand, held about 5s with no motion.
Split-screen panels opening one by one (two or three) work as a build device in a 1.4s-shot film; use only between 12-15s, not throughout.
